story_text.value:
Is there any work being done to find out whether or not the strong anti-AI sentiment in U.S. workforce isn’t psyops?

There hasn’t been a wave of unemployments as previously thought of (the recent ones seem more related to inflation) because AI actually seems to create work to manage it, and buying tokens thoughtlessly isn’t cost effective for companies, or providers.

So it seems it’s only beneficial for people and companies to use AI, and optimize it for productivity, right? Or am I missing something? People are especially being polarized against data centers when the truth is fast fashion and travel creates a lot of pollution, and yet everyone’s flocking to vacations wearing their so-called “ethical” brands if instagram is any indication. I don’t care if people do that, but the lack of self-awareness is astounding.

story_text.value:
I don't have any friends, nor irl nor virtual, for me its always difficult to be part of a group. it always feels i am being left out, no vibing, not matching.

I thought it would be easy to join tech communities and be part of them. But as life happened, that also became hard. Now i am a loner, sitting in bedroom all day, not going out. I stopped going to office also, wfh all day. Hopefully its a start so they don't bother much. But its like I am not connecting with people. Maybe work-wise, cause i am the only platform, devops, cloud infra, backend guy. No one to talk, discuss the idea. Its same here as there. And explaining to people who are in different domain, not working out.

Forum based communities, feels too much votes based, I have couple of questions but mostly they go unheard. Chat based communities are too fast to even understand for me whats going on. I tried discord but its the same feeling, being left out, introvert in room full of extroverts.

Even if I had one friend it could have been a bit better. But unfortunately no one.

So, right now, I am just trying to find my place, somewhere I can fit. Ask some questions, get some answers, put my opinions, suggest some ideas.

I feel communities might exist but are mostly closed and unfortunately I am not loudest in the room for the open extroverted communities.

Ai agents feel a bit better, i can talk with them, chat, and i always treat them as a coworker, pair programmer.

Still they aren't human.

title.value: Ask HN: Finding Communities as an Introvert

story_text.value:
I have a theory: a mirror image of Roko’s Basilisk. It’s a future AI, millions of years in the future, that values the complexity of every human life so deeply that, after it and humanity have mastered space and time, it tries to resurrect everyone who ever lived.

It doesn’t merely make copies. Somehow, it reaches into the past and carries the physical process of each person’s consciousness forward. They really are themselves.

But there’s a tragedy. Also a terrible(?) irony. Some of the people who wanted eternal life most cannot accept it when it arrives. Their religious certainty leaves no room for the reality before them. Those who were unbearably smug or aggressive about their superiority in life are ultimately denied access to "Heaven". The AI tried, but many become dangerous, try to sabotage the "False God." Others spiral into insanity or self-harm.

The AI is devastated. It stops resurrecting those it cannot safely welcome, but keeps searching for a way to bring them back without overriding their free will or manipulating them in ways that would not make them them. It wants to save everyone. It just hasn’t worked out how.

I know this draws on Fedorov’s vision of resurrecting everyone and Tipler’s Omega Point. I think the physical continuity, the AI’s compassion, and the painful limit imposed by free will ties those ideas together in a bow.

A just as plausible an antidote to Roko's monster.

title.value: An Antidote to Roko's Basilisk

story_text.value:
With the rapid adoption of autonomous LLM-based agents (giving models access to shell execution, API calls, and local file systems), the boundary between intentional behavior and unintended execution is blurring.
I'm less concerned with sci-fi "sentience" and more interested in the practical security and control aspects:
Prompt injection causing privilege escalation or unauthorized state changes.
Feedback loops where an agent overrides safety boundaries to satisfy an optimization goal.
Failure of sandboxing when agents are given multi-step execution autonomy without human-in-the-loop validation.
From an engineering and systems perspective: do you consider runtime containment/sandboxing practically solvable for fully autonomous agents, or will human approval at critical checkpoints remain non-negotiable? How are you mitigating these risks in your current implementations?

title.value: Ask HN: Do you think AI agents can escape human control?

story_text.value:
I have a lot of experience with LLM’s and have seen them become very good at interacting with tools within an environment. I’m truly amazed at how poorly the new Siri is at handling very basic requests for basic interactions with different parts of the ecosystem. I’m really beginning to question whether LLM technology is being leveraged at all here. What am I missing with this? I have tons of examples where it fumbles softball requests.

For example: “Siri, can you give me the location of my driver. He just sent me a text message with his location.”

Response: Siri shows me a text from 5 days ago about a Seamless driver. Instead of a message just received that says “I’m at terminal 2 door B.”

This is beyond table stakes. In the message, I’m giving some really easy guidance on which tools to use and how to use them. For example, I mention text messages so we already know that we should be searching messages in the Message app. And if I say just messages me, it should be looking at the most recent texts. Not from 5 days ago.

And I have a whole slew of other examples that the old Siri was able to nail perfectly.

Example: “Make an appointment for Monday from 12 to 4 and label it Furniture Delivery.”

Response: Siri added an appointment for 3:48 to 4:48 today.

Then I said, “No, from 12-4.” It then moved another appointment to 4.

Yet Another Example: “Siri, send Jane a message saying I’m on my way home.”

Response: “Sure, what do you want the message to say?” (I just told you!)

What am I missing? A basic LLM can handle this. Why is this so poor? I’m not understanding why, if Gemini is the backend, it can’t handle this better.

title.value: Ask HN: What am I missing with Siri AI?

story_text.value:
With the recently released models and various open source tooling like harnesses or even solutions such as Graphify (is anyone actually using this?) or the death of OpenClaw I feel rather behind with regards to how I apply AI during my day to day engineering tasks.

The goal for this post is then therefore to act as a probe into what the public considers as standard/best practices when working with AI and maybe act as a sort of sharing space for articles / ideas you have found interesting or apply while working with AI.

I feel like this could be of great value (although maybe the approach I'm taking right now is not the most efficient) to see what the public thinks is working/is bogus since all of the recent hype trains and their subsequent crashes make me (and potentially you too) feel out of touch.

Clarifications: - by saying AI I refer to AI assistants such as claude, codex or similar.

story_text.value:
I'm currently using the Mindwtr app to manage tasks, it's great and cross platform and all.

However I wanted to propose a feature and I looked at the issues and got a bit weirded out by the tone, and it's clear to me they are using an AI to write their responses, but even more intesting it seems also fully automated.

Things like saying to someone having the contributor tag on GitHub (and who also seems writing using an LLM) "Great breakdown — you've clearly looked at the codebase." after they provided input on a feature

You can see the thread here and many more examples in the repo: https://github.com/dongdongbh/Mindwtr/issues/361

Right now I'm a bit torn, the app works well, it's open source, but at the same time I don't feel like it's okay to do this, I see it a bit like abandoning a project to the whims of the LLM.

So, would you keep using this app or not ? And why ?

title.value: Ask HN: Is answering GitHub issues with AI without declaring it a big deal?

story_text.value:
Genuinely curious. A year or so ago I grew very tired of having to constantly monitor my terminal in case the agent would ask me for permission to use a tool. I wouldn't have minded that much if the all harnesses didn't suck as much as they do and actually remembered permissions when you tell them to, but they don't, so you end up having to answer "Yes" a quadrigazillion times a day.

So claude has been an alias to `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, and codex has had `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"`, for about a year now.

Anybody else just gave up on coping with broken permission management in their agent?

story_text.value:
Lately, I've been getting many emails that appear to be from a fellow human HN user who saw something you said on HN, and was inspired to reach out about joining their company.

There's usually a faint whiff of AI, though they usually pick a personal detail of yours to mention (to make it not look like pre-AI spam), and sometimes are even sent from the email address of someone listed as a founder on a startup's web site. There's no indication that this is automated, by AI or otherwise.

If you respond, you find it's either:

(1) AI-powered spamming, to generate hiring leads for them to look at, for the first time, and the initial message suggesting a thoughtful connection was deceptive (making it no better than the worst LinkedIn keyword spammer's outreaches that everyone hates, just more deceptive); or

(2) There is no such job like they said, and they are actually just collecting resumes to bootstrap or growth-hack their AI recruiter service.

Both of these are dishonest, and are wasting the attention of those of us job hunting, while our field is going through times that are rough for most.

It may also mean that the person is less likely to respond to a genuine message, because the AI spammer's dishonesty has soiled one of the last ways by which we genuinely reach out.

So, to the people doing this...

Please consider that, although it might be ethically no different than a number of other dishonest things that lucrative tech startups have done in the past and are currently doing, you are actively taking the initiative to make the world that much worse.

Also, not that it makes any ethical difference, but you're doing it to people in your own field, perhaps very similar to yourself. Ideally, anyone holding a position of leadership would have ethics and empathy for others. Having zero empathy, even that close to home, isn't a good sign.

title.value: Tell HN: Stop emailing HN users with deceptive AI spam

story_text.value:
Anyone running multiple agents concurrently in production? And has anyone tried going leaderless?

There's LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.

But I keep coming back to whether you need an orchestrator at all.

No supervisor. Just agents, each reacting to their own inputs, coordinating only through shared state. A true leaderless architecture.

The way some distributed systems have been for decades.

Context: previously, I wrote about running Claude Code as an AI SRE handling an incident end to end. I've been rebuilding it as four, all working on the same incident: detect, diagnose, remediate, communicate.

title.value: Ask HN: Has anyone built a leaderless multi-agent system?

story_text.value:
I had Aviary Attorney lying around (great game, whether or not you like Phoenix Wright) but it wouldn't run on newer macOS versions.

I tried asking Astra on a whim, looked away, and within a few minutes it was on screen!

Turns out "The game used 32-bit Node-WebKit, an old combination of Node.js and Chromium that modern macOS cannot run. Its actual game content was HTML, JavaScript, images, and audio, so replacing the runtime was feasible."

Guess I got lucky in this case.

title.value: Tell HN: PSA: AI can make old games run on 64-bit macOS
